key_insight: K/Rb-based double perovskite beta2SnGeX6 is a thermodynamically stable, lead-free halide family whose bandgap and thermoelectric performance can be tuned strongly by changing X = Cl, Br, I.
engineering_relevance: These materials are promising for next-generation photovoltaic absorbers, tandem/near-IR optoelectronics, and high-temperature waste-heat recovery with low toxicity.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) for structure, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Elastic-constant analysis to assess mechanical stability and ductility
Thermodynamic descriptors such as formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds are stable and cubic, with direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 eV to 0.64 eV and a peak ZT of 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The reported performance is computational, so experimental synthesis, defect tolerance, and temperature-dependent stability still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
